missions.title: The 30-Minute Warning
missions.crisis: Protons reach the Moon within tens of minutes of the flare; one astronaut is outside and external power gear is still switched on.

A Evacuate.gain: Crew is inside before the storm (only a short rover drive, ~10 mSv).
A Evacuate.cost: Outside power gear is left switched on and gets damaged (-12).
A Evacuate.real: Spacecraft are put in safe mode during radiation storms; in the Oct 2003 storms Mars Odyssey and Genesis went into safe mode.

B Secure Equip.gain: Outside gear is shut down safely (only -2).
B Secure Equip.cost: Two crew stay out ~20 min longer in suits (-5 = ~50 mSv); rover and shutdown use 4 kWh.
B Secure Equip.real: A suit (~0.4 g/cm²) lets through about 2.5x the dose of habitat walls (Townsend 1988: 311 vs 125 rem behind 1 vs 5 g/cm²).

missions.title: The Shelter Problem
missions.crisis: The storm arrives. Behind standard walls (~5 g/cm²) the crew would get ~150 mSv. Each option shows the dose that still gets through.

A Deep Shelter.gain: Cheapest option: only the shelter fans (-1); no outside work, no hardware wear, no water.
A Deep Shelter.real: Inner module is about 10 g/cm² of shielding; dose-vs-shielding curve from Townsend 1988 (NASA TM-100620).

B Pile Regolith.gain: Best protection: only ~15 mSv gets through (-1).
B Pile Regolith.cost: Rover pushes regolith bags into place (8 kWh); abrasive dust wears seals and filters (-8).
B Pile Regolith.real: 10 cm of regolith (1.5 g/cm³) adds 15 g/cm². Apollo dust clogged, scratched and broke seals (Gaier 2005, NASA TM-2005-213610).

C Water Shield.gain: Good protection (~30 mSv, -3) with no hardware wear.
C Water Shield.cost: 100 kg of water is pumped into soft bags (2 kWh) and must be re-treated before drinking (-20).
C Water Shield.real: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1: storm shelter of 10 g/cm² water-equivalent; 10 cm of water = 100 kg per m², about one layer over the crew's torsos.

missions.title: Blackout
missions.crisis: Inverters fail and the base runs on battery. Life support needs ~3 kW, the greenhouse another ~3 kW.

A Greenhouse Off.gain: Lowest battery use (-10): only life support runs.
A Greenhouse Off.cost: Crops get no light or heat (-20).
A Greenhouse Off.real: Lettuce needs 16 h of light a day; each lost light hour costs about 1.5 h of growth (NASA BVAD).

B Backup Power.gain: Everything stays on; crops are not hurt.
B Backup Power.cost: Uses the most energy (-15) and drains the emergency battery bank too deep (-8).
B Backup Power.real: NASA battery sizing caps discharge at 80%; deeper use shortens battery life (Kleinhenz & Paz 2021). CO₂ scrubber 1.0 kW, water recycler 0.74 kW.

C Brownout All.gain: Middle path: crops keep half their light (only -8).
C Brownout All.cost: Still a big battery draw (-13); cabin cools to ~18 °C and the crew sleeps badly (-2).
C Brownout All.real: NASA's comfort zone is 20-25 °C. On Apollo 13 the powered-down cabin got so cold that sleep was hard.

missions.title: Oxygen Countdown
missions.crisis: The oxygen reserve is falling: 5 crew breathe about 4.5 kg of O₂ a day.

A Bottled O2.gain: No power or water used; O₂ almost holds (-3).
A Bottled O2.cost: The emergency cylinders are used up, so nothing is left for the next emergency (-8).
A Bottled O2.real: Each kg of O₂ in high-pressure tanks needs about 1.45 kg of tank (NASA BVAD).

B Electrolysis.gain: Makes ~2.7 kg of fresh O₂, so the bar rises (+5).
B Electrolysis.cost: Splitting water needs ~5 kWh per kg of O₂ (-14). The water cost is small: 3 kg (-1).
B Electrolysis.real: ISS oxygen generator makes up to 9.2 kg O₂/day; 1.13 kg water per kg O₂; 4.7-5.5 kWh per kg O₂ (Colozza 2020). Hydrogen comes out too and must never enter the air line.

missions.title: The Water Trap
missions.crisis: Water cleaning runs at 50% because sediment clogged the filter.

A Stored Potable.gain: No power used; the filter is cleaned properly while it rests (+3).
A Stored Potable.cost: Uses 50 kg of stored water, 4 days of drinking for 5 crew (-10).
A Stored Potable.real: Each astronaut needs at least 2.5 L of water a day for drinking and food (NASA OCHMO-TB-027).

B Melt Crater Ice.gain: The only option that adds water (+10, ~80 kg melted).
B Melt Crater Ice.cost: Melting very cold ice takes ~0.19 kWh per kg (-15); sediment hits the filter again (-5).
B Melt Crater Ice.real: Warm ice from about -170 °C, melt it (334 kJ/kg), warm to 20 °C: about 0.19 kWh per kg (our calculation).

C Drink Priority.gain: Crew water is safe at almost no cost (-3).
C Drink Priority.cost: Crops get no water for the day (-10).
C Drink Priority.real: Lettuce uses about 2.1 kg of water per m² per day (NASA BVAD), so 20 m² needs ~42 kg a day.

missions.title: The Last Harvest
missions.crisis: The nutrient pump has failed and the crops are wilting.

A Restore Loop.gain: Crops recover (+10) and the next harvest is saved (+6 food).
A Restore Loop.cost: Pumps and lights need ~12 kWh; the loop needs 30 kg of water (-6).
A Restore Loop.real: Grow lights for 20 m² of lettuce are about 3 kW (LED, ~0.15 kW/m², from NASA BVAD values).

B Abandon Crops.gain: Frees the greenhouse power for the night (+8).
B Abandon Crops.cost: Crops die (-35) and the next harvest is lost (-8 food).
B Abandon Crops.real: 20 m² of lettuce gives about 73 kg of fresh food per 28-day cycle (NASA BVAD yield).

missions.title: The Critical Failure
missions.crisis: Power Bus Junction 4 is overheating and arcing.

A Isolate Bus.gain: Fastest and safest; little power lost (-3).
A Isolate Bus.cost: Module 4 stays dead until a later repair (-12).
A Isolate Bus.real: In 2012 a failed ISS power box (MBSU-1) cut 2 of 8 power channels; the station ran on about 75% power until it was fixed.

B Manual Repair.gain: The junction is fixed; hardware improves (+10).
B Manual Repair.cost: Test and repair use 10 kWh; crew works near hot, smoking parts (-4).
B Manual Repair.real: Sunita Williams and Akihiko Hoshide replaced that ISS power box on two spacewalks in Aug-Sep 2012, after a stuck bolt.

C Reroute Bus.gain: Module 4 keeps working; little hardware loss (-3).
C Reroute Bus.cost: The other junction is overloaded and wastes power (-8); the greenhouse is cut first (-8).
C Reroute Bus.real: Real power systems shed the least important loads first to keep life support running.

missions.title: The Final Decision
missions.crisis: The storm is passing, but proton levels can stay high for hours.

A Hold Shelter.gain: Crew rests and avoids the storm's tail (+3).
A Hold Shelter.cost: Shelter life support keeps running on battery (-6) and uses water (-2).
A Hold Shelter.real: NOAA: a solar radiation storm can last from hours to days.

B Controlled Recovery.gain: Crew resets the inverters: solar power comes back (+15) and systems are repaired (+6).
B Controlled Recovery.cost: Crew gets some leftover radiation while working outside (-5).
B Controlled Recovery.real: Same NOAA fact: leaving early means some extra dose.
